Record An Audiobook Chapter For LibriVox

Read a chapter of a public domain book aloud and it becomes a free audiobook for anyone who can't read print.

Cost
Free
Time
90-120 min
People
Solo / Duo, Small Group (3-6)
Where
Home
Bring
A quiet room, a decent microphone or headset

Why this matters

Commercial audiobooks are expensive and cover only a fraction of what's been written, leaving blind, low-vision and dyslexic readers with far less access to literature than everyone else. LibriVox recordings are free and public domain forever. Because books are recorded chapter by chapter by different volunteers, one evening's work genuinely completes a piece of something permanent.

How to do it

Go to LibriVox and look at the projects currently seeking readers. Books are split into chapters and claimed individually, so you're committing to one chapter rather than a whole novel.

You'll need: - A quiet room. Soft furnishings help enormously - recording in a room with curtains, carpet and a bed is much better than a bare kitchen. - A decent USB microphone or a wired headset. Laptop built-in mics are usually too noisy. - Free recording software like Audacity.

The process: - Claim a chapter in the forum, record it, and upload. A proof-listener checks it and flags anything to redo. - Read slower than feels natural. Almost everyone reads too fast on a first attempt. - Leave a few seconds of silence at the start and end, and pause rather than restarting when you stumble - it's much easier to edit out a gap than a repeated word. - Read the whole chapter through beforehand so you're not sight-reading names and unfamiliar words.

Non-native accents are welcome - the catalogue is deliberately varied and there's no house style.

Doing it with friends works well: each of you claims a different chapter of the same book and you finish something together.
